# L-105643 — Parent–derivative height flow is generated by the actual Turán quotient

Claim ID: `L-105643`  
Status: **PROVED EXACT ARGUMENT-PRINCIPLE / PHASE-FLOW IDENTITY**  
Created: 2026-08-25  
Depends on: `L-105602`, `L-105613`, `L-105640--L-105642`; sibling `L-106400--L-106431`  
RH status: **not assumed**

## 1. One two-rung height all-pass

Let `F` be a real entire function.  At a regular height `H>0`, define

\[
\Theta_{F,H}(x)
={F(x+iH)\over F(x-iH)},
\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\tag{L-105643.1}
\]

and the parent–derivative quotient

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R_{F,H}(x)
={\Theta_{F,H}(x)\over\Theta_{F',H}(x)}
={F(x+iH)F'(x-iH)
 \over F(x-iH)F'(x+iH)}.
}
\tag{L-105643.2}
\]

Every boundary value is unimodular.  Common parent/derivative factors are
cancelled before assigning a meromorphic index.

For a polynomial compactified on the full real line,

\[
\deg\Theta_{F,H}=-N_F(H),
\]

where `N_F(H)` counts zeros in `|Im rho|<H`.  Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\deg\mathcal R_{F,H}
=N_{F'}(H)-N_F(H).
}
\tag{L-105643.3}
\]

The same identity holds in a finite regular entire-function rectangle with the
explicit vertical-side term retained.  Along a derivative ladder, all
intermediate height phases telescope.

## 2. Exact continuous phase generator

Away from parent and derivative zeros, differentiate in height.  Reality gives

\[
\partial_H\arg\Theta_{F,H}(x)
=2\operatorname{Re}{F'(x+iH)\over F(x+iH)}.
\tag{L-105643.4}
\]

Subtracting the derivative phase yields

\[
\boxed{
\partial_H\arg\mathcal R_{F,H}(x)
=2\operatorname{Re}
\left(
{F'\over F}-{F''\over F'}
\right)(x+iH).
}
\tag{L-105643.5}
\]

Since

\[
{F'\over F}-{F''\over F'}
={F'^2-FF''\over FF'},
\]

one has the exact Turán form

\[
\boxed{
\partial_H\arg\mathcal R_{F,H}(x)
=2\operatorname{Re}
{\mathcal L_F(x+iH)
 \over F(x+iH)F'(x+iH)},
\qquad
\mathcal L_F=F'^2-FF''.
}
\tag{L-105643.6}
\]

Thus the actual Laguerre–Turán function is not merely a favorable endpoint
numerator.  After division by the literal parent and derivative traces, it is
the infinitesimal generator of the complete signed two-rung height flow.

## 3. Exact divisor and residue signs

Meromorphically,

\[
\boxed{
{\mathcal L_F\over FF'}
=\partial_z\log{F\over F'}.
}
\tag{L-105643.7}
\]

Consequently:

```text
parent zero of multiplicity m:      residue +m;
derivative zero of multiplicity n:  residue -n;
common factor:                      cancels confluently.
```

At a simple parent zero `rho`,

\[
{\mathcal L_F\over FF'}(z)
={1\over z-\rho}+O(1),
\]

whereas at a simple noncommon derivative zero `c`,

\[
{\mathcal L_F\over FF'}(z)
=-{1\over z-c}+O(1).
\]

The parent Clark atom and the derivative anti-inner factor are therefore the
two opposite residues of one physical meromorphic current.

## 4. Distributional spectral flow

As `H` crosses a regular zero height, the degree in (L-105643.3) jumps by the
corresponding residue multiplicity:

```text
parent zero crosses:       degree decreases by its multiplicity;
derivative zero crosses:   degree increases by its multiplicity.
```

Between crossing heights the degree is constant; the spatial integral of the
continuous phase generator has zero net derivative after endpoint terms are
included.  At a crossing, the rank-one or confluent model-space flux of
`L-105640` supplies the missing distributional atom.

Thus the exact height ledger is

\[
\boxed{
\text{continuous Turán phase flow}
+
\text{boundary model-space atoms}
=
\text{parent-minus-derivative zero index}.
}
\tag{L-105643.8}
\]

No separate `PARENTATOM` correction is mathematically necessary once the
signed two-rung phase is retained.

## 5. Xi specialization

For `F=Xi`,

\[
\widehat{\mathcal L_\Xi}(\xi)
={1\over4\pi}
\int(2u-\xi)^2\Phi(u)\Phi(\xi-u)d\xi
\ge0
\]

with the integration variable interpreted as in `L-105613`.  Hence the same
actual positive exterior-square source which drives the current hierarchy is
the generator of the signed parent/derivative height index.

The pointwise and topological programmes now share the complete literal
object:

```text
continuous source:      L_Xi = Xi'^2-Xi Xi'';
physical denominator:   Xi Xi';
boundary atoms:          zeros of Xi minus zeros of Xi';
finite consumer:         signed all-pass/model-space index.
```

## 6. Scope

Positivity of the Fourier density of `L_Xi` does not sign the physical quotient
`L_Xi/(Xi Xi')`.  The theorem does not bound its height integral, exclude a
parent Xi boundary zero, or prove that derivative atoms compensate parent
atoms.  It proves that these formerly separate tasks are one signed spectral
flow and must be estimated before either residue family is discarded.  RH
remains unproved.
